51.text: Which of the following does not come under the Class Mammals?
51.sol: Lamprey (or Petromyzon) belongs to class cyclostomata. The lamprey has about \(1 \mathrm{~m}\). long greenish brown, cylindrical body with smooth, scaleless, slimy skin; anterior circular, jawless mouth; a single dorsal naris; seven pairs of circular gill slits; 2 dorsal fins and a tail fin. Its life cycle includes two quite different phases. The larval phase (called ammocoete) is a fresh water sedentary, filter feeding and microphagus creature reminiscent of the lancet. The fish like adult lives in the sea and is parasitic on fishes.

6676.text: If $x=\frac{1}{5}+\frac{1.3}{5.10}+\frac{1.3.5}{5.10.5}+\ldots \infty$, then $3 x^2+6 x$ is equal to
6676.sol:
Given that,
$\begin{aligned}
& x=\frac{1}{5}+\frac{1 \cdot 3}{5 \cdot 10}+\frac{1 \cdot 3 \cdot 5}{5 \cdot 10 \cdot 5}+\cdots \\
& =\frac{1}{5}+\frac{1 \cdot 3}{2 \times 1}\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)^2+\frac{1 \cdot 3 \cdot 5}{3 \times 2 \times 1}\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)^3+\cdots \\
& =\frac{1}{5}+\frac{1 \cdot 3}{2 !}\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)^2+\frac{1 \cdot 3 \cdot 5}{3 !}\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)^3+\cdots
\end{aligned}$
On adding 1 both the sides, we get
$1+x=1+\frac{1}{5}+\frac{1 \cdot 3}{2 !}\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)^2+\frac{1 \cdot 3 \cdot 5}{3 !}\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)^3+\cdots$
Now,
According to the binomial theorem for any index,
$\begin{aligned}
& \left(1-\frac{2}{5}\right)^{-1 / 2}=1+\frac{1}{5}+\frac{1 \cdot 3}{2 !}\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)^2+\frac{1 \cdot 3 \cdot 5}{3 !}\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)^3+\cdots \\
& 1+x=\left(1-\frac{2}{5}\right)^{-1 / 2} \Rightarrow 1+x=\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)^{-1 / 2} \\
& 1+x=\left(\frac{5}{3}\right)^{1 / 2} \\
& (1+x)^2=\frac{5}{3} \\
& 1+2 x+x^2=\frac{5}{3} \\
& 3+6 x+3 x^2=5 \\
& 3 x^2+6 x=2
\end{aligned}$

7336.subject: Mathematics
7336.sol:
Let

$C = \mathop{∑}_{n = 0}^{\infty}\dfrac{cosn\theta}{{2}^{n}}$

$⇒ C = 1 + \dfrac{cos\left(\theta\right)}{2} + \dfrac{cos\left(2\theta\right)}{{2}^{2}} + \dfrac{cos\left(3\theta\right)}{{2}^{3}} + . . . .$

$iS = \dfrac{isin\left(\theta\right)}{2} + \dfrac{isin\left(2\theta\right)}{{2}^{2}} + \dfrac{isin\left(3\theta\right)}{{2}^{3}} + . . . .$

Then,

$C + iS = 1 + \dfrac{1}{2}\left(cos\theta + isin\theta\right) + \dfrac{1}{{2}^{2}}\left(cos2\theta + isin2\theta\right) + \dfrac{1}{{2}^{3}}\left(cos3\theta + isin3\theta\right) + . . . .$

$⇒ C + iS = 1 + \dfrac{1}{2}{e}^{i\theta} + \dfrac{1}{{2}^{2}}{e}^{2i\theta} + \dfrac{1}{{2}^{3}}{e}^{3i\theta} + . . . . . .$

$⇒ C + iS = 1 + \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2}{e}^{i\theta}}{1 - \dfrac{1}{2}{e}^{i\theta}}$

$⇒ C + iS = 1 + \dfrac{{e}^{i\theta}}{2 - {e}^{i\theta}}$

$⇒ C + iS = 1 + \dfrac{cos\theta + isin\theta}{2 - cos\theta - isin\theta}$

$⇒ C + iS = 1 + \left[\left(\dfrac{cos\theta + isin\theta}{2 - cos\theta - isin\theta}\right) \times \left(\dfrac{2 - cos\theta + isin\theta}{2 - cos\theta + isin\theta}\right)\right]$

$⇒ C + iS = 1 + \left[\dfrac{cos\theta\left(2 - cos\theta + isin\theta\right) + isin\theta\left(2 - cos\theta + isin\theta\right)}{{\left(2 - cos\theta\right)}^{2} + {sin}^{2}\theta}\right]$

$⇒ C + iS = 1 + \left[\dfrac{2cos\theta - {cos}^{2}\theta - {sin}^{2}\theta + 2isin\theta}{5 - 4cos\theta}\right]$

$⇒ C + iS = 1 + \left[\dfrac{2cos\theta - 1 + 2isin\theta}{5 - 4cos\theta}\right]$

$⇒ C + iS = \left[\dfrac{4 - 2cos\theta + 2isin\theta}{5 - 4cos\theta}\right]$

$⇒ C + iS = \left(\dfrac{4 - 2cos\theta}{5 - 4cos\theta}\right) + i\left(\dfrac{2sin\theta}{5 - 4cos\theta}\right)$

On comparing real and imaginary part, we get

$C = \dfrac{4 - 2cos\theta}{5 - 4cos\theta}$

By using Baye's theorem,

11541.sol:
Since $\sin ^2 18^{{}^{\circ}}$ and $\cos ^2 36^{{}^{\circ}}$ are the roots of a quadratic equation.
$\therefore \text{ Sum of roots }=\sin ^2 18^{{}^{\circ}}+\cos ^2 36^{{}^{\circ}}=\left(\frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{4}\right)^2+\left(\frac{\sqrt{5}+1}{4}\right)^2=\frac{5+1-2 \sqrt{5}}{16}+\frac{5+1+2 \sqrt{5}}{16}=\frac{12}{16}=\frac{3}{4}$
and product of roots $=\sin ^2 18^{{}^{\circ}} \cdot \cos ^2 36^{{}^{\circ}}=\left(\frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{4}\right)^2\left(\frac{\sqrt{5}+1}{4}\right)^2=\left(\frac{5-1}{4 \times 4}\right)^2=\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)^2=\frac{1}{16}$
Required equation whose roots are $\sin ^2 18^{{}^{\circ}}$ and $\cos ^2 36^{{}^{\circ}}$, is
$x^2-(\text{ sum of roots }) x+(\text{ product of roots })=0\Rightarrow \quad x^2-\frac{3}{4} x+\frac{1}{16}=0\Rightarrow \quad 16 x^2-12 x+1=0$

13188.text: Let $(\vec{a}, \vec{b})$ denote the angle between vectors $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$. If $\vec{a}=2 \hat{i}+3 \hat{j}+6 \hat{k}, \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}=4$ and $(\vec{a}, \vec{b})=\cos ^{-1} \left(\frac{4}{21}\right), then $\overline{$\mathrm{a}$}+\overline{$\mathrm{b}$}=$$
13188.sol:
$\begin{aligned}
& \bar{a}=2 \hat{i}+3 \hat{j}+6 \hat{k} \Rightarrow|\bar{a}|=7 \\
& \bar{a} \cdot \bar{b}=4 \\
& \Rightarrow|\bar{a}| \cdot|\bar{b}| \cos \theta=4 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 7 \cdot|\bar{b}| \times \frac{4}{21}=4 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 7 \times|\bar{b}| \times \frac{1}{21}=1 \Rightarrow|\bar{b}|=3 . \\
& \therefore|\bar{a}+\bar{b}|^2=|\bar{a}|^2+|\bar{b}|^2+2 \bar{a} \cdot \bar{b} \\
& \Rightarrow|\bar{a}+\bar{b}|^2=49+9+2 \times 4=66 \\
& \Rightarrow|\bar{a}+\bar{b}|^2=\sqrt{66} .
\end{aligned}$
Let us check option (a) :
$|\bar{a}+\bar{b}|=\sqrt{(3)^2+1+64} \neq \sqrt{66}$
(not correct)
Let us check option (b) :
$|\bar{a}+\bar{b}|=\sqrt{9+25+16} \neq \sqrt{66}$
(not correct)
Let us check option (c) :
$|\bar{a}+\bar{b}|=\sqrt{9+25+64} \neq \sqrt{66}$
(not correct)
Let us check option (d) :
$|\bar{a}+\bar{b}|=\sqrt{1+1+64}=\sqrt{66}$
(correct)

13283.text: Let $\overset{→}{u} = 2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}, \overset{→}{v} = - 3\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j}$ and $\overset{→}{w} = \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}$, Then which of the following statement is true?
13283.sol:
$\overset{→}{u} = 2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}, \overset{→}{v} = - 3\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j}$, $\overset{→}{w} = \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{→}{u}. \overset{→}{v} = \left(2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right). \left(-3\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j}\right)$

$⇒ \overset{→}{u}. \overset{→}{v} = - 6 + 6 + 0$

$⇒ \overset{→}{u}. \overset{→}{v} = 0$

Therefore. $\overset{→}{u}$ is perpendicular to $\overset{→}{v}$.

Now, $\overset{→}{u}. \overset{→}{w} = ( 2\overset{^}{i}. \overset{^}{i} ) + ( 3\overset{^}{j}. - \overset{^}{j} ) + ( \overset{^}{k}. 4\overset{^}{k} )$

$⇒ \overset{→}{u}. \overset{→}{w} = 2 - 3 + 4 = 3$

Therefore, $\overset{→}{u}$ is not perpendicular $\overset{→}{w}$.

Now, $\overset{→}{w}. \overset{→}{v} = \left(\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} +4\overset{^}{k}\right). \left(-3\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j}\right)$

$⇒ \overset{→}{w}. \overset{→}{v} = - 3 - 2 + 0 = - 5$

Therefore $\overset{→}{w}$ is not perpendicular $\overset{→}{v}$.

15477.text: Two soap bubbles combine to form a single bubble. In this process, the change in volume and surface area are respectively $V$ and $A$. If $P$ is the atmospheric pressure, and $T$ is the surface tension of the soap solution, the following relation is true :
15477.sol:
Let radii of two soap bubbles are $a$ and $b$ respectively and radius of single larger bubble is $c$.
As excess pressure for a soap bubble is $\frac{4 T}{r}$ and external pressure $P$.
$P_i=P+\frac{4 T}{r}$
So, $\quad P_a=P+\frac{4 T}{a}, P_b=P+\frac{4 T}{b}$
and $\quad P_c=P+\frac{4 T}{c}$ ...(i)
and $\quad V_a=\frac{4}{3} \pi a^3, \quad V_b=\frac{4}{3} \pi b^3$
and $\quad V_c=\frac{4}{3} \pi c^3$ ...(ii)
Now as mass is conserved.
$\mu_a+\mu_b=\mu_c$
i.e., $\quad \frac{P_a V_a}{R T_a}+\frac{P_b V_b}{R T_b}=\frac{P_c V_c}{R T_c} \quad($ as $P V=\mu R T)$
As temperature is constant, i.e., $T_a=T_b=T_c$
So, $\quad P_a V_a+P_b V_b=P_c V_c$
which in the light of Eqs. (i) and (ii) becomes,
$\left(P+\frac{4 T}{a}\right) \left(\frac{4}{3} \pi$ a^3\right)+ $\left(P+\frac{4 T}{b}\right)$\$left(\frac{4}{3} \pib^3\right)= \$ lleft(P+$\frac{4 T}{c}\right)\left(\frac{4}{3} \pic^3\right)$
i.e., $4 T  \left(a²+b²-c²\right)=P  \left($ c^3-a³-b³\right)$ ...(iii)
Now, $\quad  V=$\frac{4}{3} \pi\left($ a^3+b³-c³\right)$ 
and $\quad A=4 $\pi\left($ a^2+b²-c²\right)\therefore \quad $\frac{T A}{\pi}=-\frac{3}{4 \pi}$ V P$
or $\quad 4 T A+3 P V=0$$

15561.text: Two wires of equal length and equal cross sectional areas are suspended as shown in the figure. Their Young's modulii are \(Y_1\) and \(Y_2\), respectively. The equivalent Young's modulus is
15561.sol:
Given, two wires have same length and equal cross-sectional area.

i.e., \(l_1=l_2=l\) and \(A_1=A_2=A\)
Suppose, \(m\) is the mass of the hanging load.
From figure, \(2 T=m g\)
i.e.,
\$T=\frac{m g}{2}$
Hence, stress on each wire \$=\frac{T}{A}=\frac{m g}{2 A}$
\(\therefore \quad Y_1=\frac{\text{ stress }}{\text{ strain }}=\frac{\frac{m g}{2 A}}{\frac{\Delta l}{l}}=\frac{m g l}{2 A \Delta l}\)...(i)
and \$ Y_2=\frac{\text{ stress }}{\text{ strain }}=\frac{\frac{m g}{2 A}}{\frac{\Delta l}{l}}=\frac{m g l}{2 A \Delta l}$...(ii)
If \(Y\) be the equivalent Young's modulus of the combination,
then, \(\quad Y=\frac{m g l}{A \Delta l}\)...(iii)
From Eqs. (i), (ii) and (iii), we get
\$ Y=\frac{Y_1+Y_2}{2}$

18278.text: Let $f: R \to R$ be a function satisfying $f\left(x + y\right) = f\left(x\right) + 2y^{2} + kxy$ for all $x, y \in \mathbb{R}$. If $f  \left(1\right) = 2$ and $f\left(2\right) = 8$, then $f\left(x\right) is equal to$
18278.sol:
We have, $f\left(x + y\right) = f\left(x\right) + 2{y}^{2} + kxy$ for all $x, y \in R$

$⇒ \dfrac{f\left(x + y\right) - f\left(x\right)}{y} = 2y + kx$ for all $x \in R$

$⇒ \lim_{y \to 0}\dfrac{f\left(x + y\right) - f\left(x\right)}{y} = \lim_{y \to 0}\left(2y + kx\right)$

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(x\right) = kx$ for all $x \in R$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{k{x}^{2}}{2} + C$ for all $x \in R$  [by integration]

But $f\left(1\right) = 2$ and $f\left(2\right) = 8$

$∴ 2 = \dfrac{k}{2} + C$ and $8 = 2k + C$

$k = 4$ and $C = 0$

Hence, $f\left(x\right) = 2{x}^{2}$ for all $x \in R$

So, option (a) is correct.

19515.subject: Chemistry
19515.text: In Friedal-Crafts alkylation reaction of phenol with chloromethane, the product formed will be
19515.sol:
Phenol is an electron-rich aromatic compound due to the presence of the hydroxyl group, which is strongly activating and ortho/para-directing.

Friedel-Crafts alkylation involves the reaction of an aromatic ring with an alkyl halide in the presence of a Lewis acid catalyst like $AlCl_{3}$.

However, phenol reacts with the Lewis acid catalyst to form a phenoxide-aluminum complex. This complex deactivates the ring towards electrophilic substitution and makes the reaction difficult.

Despite this, under specific conditions, the electrophilic substitution occurs at the ortho and para positions due to the directing effect of the $-OH$ group.

Consequently, the reaction of phenol with chloromethane in the presence of a catalyst yields a mixture of ortho-cresol and para-cresol.

Answer: mixture of $o$-and $p$-cresol

Two statements, Assertion and Reason are given. Choose the correct option from the following.
Assertion: In the secondary structure of RNA, double helix structure is formed.
Reason: In the double structure of RNA, two nucleic acid chains are wound about each other and held together by hydrogen bonds between pairs of bases
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.
Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct.
Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.
19674.sol:
Assertion is correct: RNA is single-stranded, but its secondary structure involves the strand folding back on itself to form localised double-helical regions (e.g., stem-loops in tRNA, hairpin loops).

Reason is incorrect: The double-helical regions in RNA are formed by intramolecular hydrogen bonding within a single chain, not by two separate nucleic acid chains wound around each other. That description applies to DNA, not RNA.

Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.

20374.subject: Chemistry
20374.text:
Select the reagents needed to convert Benzene to 4–Bromophenylpropene in the correct sequential order.
(A). $\text{Cl}_2/\Delta$
(B). $(\text{CH}_3)_2$-CHCl /anhyd. $\text{AlCl}_3$
(C). Alc. KOH
(D). $\text{Br}_2$ / Fe
20374.sol:
The conversion of benzene to 4-bromophenylpropene involves the following sequential steps:

1. Friedel-Crafts Alkylation (Reagent B): Benzene reacts with isopropyl chloride in the presence of anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ to form isopropylbenzene (cumene).
$\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 + (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCl} \xrightarrow{\text{anhyd. AlCl}_3} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$

2. Electrophilic Aromatic Substitution (Reagent D): Isopropylbenzene undergoes bromination with $\text{Br}_2/\text{Fe}$. The isopropyl group is ortho/para-directing. Due to steric hindrance at the ortho position, the major product is 4-bromoisopropylbenzene.
$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2 + \text{Br}_2/\text{Fe} \rightarrow 4\text{-Br-C}_6\text{H}_4\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$

3. Free Radical Halogenation (Reagent A): Treatment with $\text{Cl}_2/\Delta$ leads to substitution at the benzylic position, replacing the tertiary benzylic hydrogen with a chlorine atom to form 1-bromo-4-(2-chloropropan-2-yl)benzene.
$4\text{-Br-C}_6\text{H}_4\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2 + \text{Cl}_2/\Delta \rightarrow 4\text{-Br-C}_6\text{H}_4\text{CCl}(\text{CH}_3)_2$

4. Dehydrohalogenation (Reagent C): Finally, reaction with alcoholic KOH causes E2 elimination of $\text{HCl}$, forming a double bond to yield 2-(4-bromophenyl)propene (a 4-bromophenylpropene derivative).
$4\text{-Br-C}_6\text{H}_4\text{CCl}(\text{CH}_3)_2 + \text{Alc. KOH} \rightarrow 4\text{-Br-C}_6\text{H}_4\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)=\text{CH}_2$

The correct sequential order of reagents is B, D, A, C.

20602.subject: Chemistry
20602.text: The vacant space in bec lattice cell is
20602.sol:
In a body-centered cubic (BCC) unit cell, the number of atoms per unit cell is $Z = 2$.

The relation between the edge length $a$ and the atomic radius $r$ is given by $4r = \sqrt{3}a$, which implies $r = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}a}{4}$.

The volume occupied by the atoms is $V_{atoms} = Z \times \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^{3} = 2 \times \dfrac{4}{3}\pi \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}a}{4}\right)^{3}$.

$V_{atoms} = 2 \times \dfrac{4}{3}\pi \times \dfrac{3\sqrt{3}a^{3}}{64} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}\pi a^{3}}{8} \approx 0.68 a^{3}$.

The packing efficiency is $68\%$.

The vacant space is $100\% - 68\% = 32\%$.

Answer: $32 \%$

20621.text:
A 5% solution (by mass) of cane sugar in water has a freezing point of 271 K. The freezing point of a 5% solution (by mass) of glucose in water is:
[freezing point of pure water: 273.15 K]
20621.sol:
Depression in freezing point is given by $\Delta T_{f} = K_{f} m$

For $5\%$ (by mass) cane sugar solution:

Mass of cane sugar $= 5$ g, Mass of water $= 95$ g

Molar mass of cane sugar $= 342$ g/mol

$\Delta T_{f1} = 273.15 - 271 = 2.15$ K

$2.15 = K_{f} \times \dfrac{5 \times 1000}{342 \times 95}$

For $5\%$ (by mass) glucose solution:

Mass of glucose $= 5$ g, Mass of water $= 95$ g

Molar mass of glucose $= 180$ g/mol

$\Delta T_{f2} = K_{f} \times \dfrac{5 \times 1000}{180 \times 95}$

Taking the ratio of $\Delta T_{f2}$ and $\Delta T_{f1}$:

$\dfrac{\Delta T_{f2}}{2.15} = \dfrac{342}{180} = 1.9$

$\Delta T_{f2} = 2.15 \times 1.9 = 4.085$ K

Freezing point of glucose solution $= 273.15 - 4.085 = 269.065$ K $\approx 269$ K

Answer: 269 K

21895.subject: Mathematics
21895.text: A person writes four letters and address four envelopes. If the letters are placed in the envelopes at random, then the probability that not all letters are placed in the right envelope is
21895.sol:
The total number of ways to place 4 letters into 4 envelopes is $4! = 24$.

The event that all letters are placed in the right envelope corresponds to exactly 1 way (each letter in its corresponding envelope).

The probability that all letters are placed in the right envelope is $P(A) = \dfrac{1}{24}$.

The probability that not all letters are placed in the right envelope is the complement of the event that all letters are placed correctly.

Therefore, the required probability is $1 - P(A) = 1 - \dfrac{1}{24} = \dfrac{23}{24}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{23}{24}$

22847.subject: Physics
22847.text: Which of the following diagram represents the variation of the electric field with distance $r$ from the centre of a uniformly charged non-conducting sphere of radius $R$ ?
22847.sol:
For a uniformly charged non-conducting sphere of radius $R$ and total charge $Q$, the electric field $E$ at a distance $r$ from the centre is determined using Gauss's Law.

Inside the sphere, where $r < R$, the electric field is given by $E = \dfrac{kQr}{R^3}$, where $k = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}$. This shows that $E$ is directly proportional to $r$, meaning the graph is a straight line passing through the origin with a positive slope.

Outside the sphere, where $r \ge R$, the sphere acts as a point charge located at its centre. The electric field is given by $E = \dfrac{kQ}{r^2}$. This shows that $E$ is inversely proportional to the square of the distance $r$, resulting in a curve that decreases as $r$ increases.

At the surface of the sphere, $r = R$, the electric field reaches its maximum value $E_\max = \dfrac{kQ}{R^2}$.

Comparing these characteristics with the given options, the graph that shows a linear increase for $r < R$ and a $1/r^2$ decrease for $r > R$ is represented in option c.

Answer:

23720.subject: Physics
23720.text: Two open organ pipes A and B of length $22 \mathrm{ cm}$ and $22.5 \mathrm{ cm}$ respectively produce 2 beats per sec when sounded together. The frequency of the shorter pipe is
23720.sol:
The fundamental frequency of an open organ pipe of length $L$ is given by $f = \dfrac{v}{2L}$, where $v$ is the speed of sound in air. Let $v = 330 \text{ m/s}$ be the standard speed of sound.

For pipe A with length $L_A = 22 \text{ cm} = 0.22 \text{ m}$, the frequency is $f_A = \dfrac{330}{2 \times 0.22} = \dfrac{330}{0.44} = 750 \text{ Hz}$.

For pipe B with length $L_B = 22.5 \text{ cm} = 0.225 \text{ m}$, the frequency is $f_B = \dfrac{330}{2 \times 0.225} = \dfrac{330}{0.45} = 733.33 \text{ Hz}$.

The beat frequency is $|f_A - f_B| = |750 - 733.33| = 16.67 \text{ Hz}$, which does not match the given 2 beats per second. This implies the speed of sound $v$ is not $330 \text{ m/s}$.

Let $f_A = \dfrac{v}{2 \times 0.22}$ and $f_B = \dfrac{v}{2 \times 0.225}$. The beat frequency is $f_A - f_B = \dfrac{v}{2} \left( \dfrac{1}{0.22} - \dfrac{1}{0.225} \right) = 2$.

Calculating the difference: $\dfrac{1}{0.22} - \dfrac{1}{0.225} = \dfrac{0.225 - 0.22}{0.22 \times 0.225} = \dfrac{0.005}{0.0495} = \dfrac{5}{49.5} = \dfrac{1}{9.9}$.

Substituting into the beat equation: $\dfrac{v}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{9.9} = 2 \Rightarrow v = 2 \times 2 \times 9.9 = 39.6 \text{ m/s}$.

The frequency of the shorter pipe A is $f_A = \dfrac{39.6}{0.44} = 90 \text{ Hz}$.

Answer: 90 Hz

25157.text:
The entropy versus temperature plot for phases $\alpha$ and $\beta$ at $1$ bar pressure is given. ${S}_{T} and {S}_{0}$ are entropies of the phases at temperatures $T and 0K$, respectively.

The transition temperature for $\alpha$ to $\beta$ phase change is 600K and ${C}_{p, \beta} - {C}_{p, \alpha} = 1J{mol}^{- 1}{K}^{- 1}$. Assume $\left({C}_{p, \beta} - {C}_{p, \alpha}\right)$ is independent of temperature in the range of $200 to 700K . {C}_{p, \alpha} and {C}_{p, \beta}$ are heat capacities of $\alpha and \beta$ phases, respectively.


The value of enthalpy change, ${H}_{\beta} - {H}_{\alpha}$ (in ${Jmol}^{- 1}$ ), at $300K$ is
25157.sol:
According to Kirchhoff's law

${\Delta H}_{{T}_{2}} - {\Delta H}_{{T}_{1}} = n \times \left({C}_{p, \beta} - {C}_{p, \alpha}\right) ( {T}_{2} - {T}_{1} )$

${\Delta H}_{600} - {\Delta H}_{300} = 1 \times \left({C}_{p, \beta} - {C}_{p, \alpha}\right) ( 600 - 300 )$

Now, at transition temperature, $∆ G = 0$

${\Delta H}_{600} = {T \Delta S}_{600}$

$= 600 \times ( 6 - 5 )$

$600 - {\Delta H}_{300} = 1 \times 1 \times 300$

${\Delta H}_{300} = 600 - 300$

$= 300J{mol}^{- 1}$

$\left({x}^{2} - 5\right)\dfrac{dy}{dx} - 2xy = - 2x{\left({x}^{2} - 5\right)}^{2}$

Which is a linear differential equation,

So, integrating factor,$\text{I.F.} = {e}^{∫ \dfrac{- 2x}{{x}^{2} - 5}dx} = \dfrac{1}{\left|{x}^{2} - 5\right|}$

Now solution of differential equation is given by,

$y ⋅ \dfrac{1}{\left|{x}^{2} - 5\right|} = ∫ - 2x ⋅ \dfrac{{x}^{2} - 5}{\left|{x}^{2} - 5\right|}dx$

$⇒ \dfrac{y}{\left|{x}^{2} - 5\right|} = \dfrac{{x}^{2} - 5}{\left|{x}^{2} - 5\right|}\left(- {x}^{2}\right) + C$

Now using the given value, $y ( 2 ) = 7 ⇒ C = 3$

$⇒ y = - {x}^{2}\left({x}^{2} - 5\right) + 3\left|{x}^{2} - 5\right|$

$⇒ y = f ( x )$ is even function

If $0 < x < \sqrt{5}, y = - {x}^{4} + 5{x}^{2} - 3{x}^{2} + 15$

$⇒ y = - {x}^{4} + 2{x}^{2} + 15$

For increasing function $\dfrac{dy}{dx} > 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = - 4{x}^{3} + 4x > 0$

$⇒ x < 1$
If $x > \sqrt{5}, y = - {x}^{4} + 5{x}^{2} + 3{x}^{2} - 15$

$⇒ y = - {x}^{4} + 8{x}^{2} - 15$
For increasing function $\dfrac{dy}{dx} > 0$

$⇒ - 4x\left({x}^{2} - 4\right) > 0$

$⇒ 4x\left({x}^{2} - 4\right) < 0$

$⇒ x \in \left(- \infty , - 2\right) ∪ \left(0, 2\right)$ but $x > \sqrt{5}$

$⇒ x = ϕ$

$⇒ y ( x )$ is increasing over $( 0, 1 )$

Now plotting the graph we get,

Hence, maximum value of the function is given by,

$⇒ f ( x{)}_{max} = 16$

${F}^{′}\left(x\right) = f ( x )$
$G\left(x\right) = \mathop{∫}_{- 1}^{x}t\left|f ( f\left(t\right) )\right|dt$ = $\mathop{∫}_{1}^{x}t\left|f ( f\left(t\right) )\right|dt$ , as it is an odd function,

$⇒ {G}^{′}\left(x\right) = x\left|f ( f\left(x\right) )\right|$
$\lim_{x \to 1} ⁡ \dfrac{F ( x )}{G ( x )} = \lim_{x \to 1} ⁡ \dfrac{F′ ( x )}{G′ ( x )} = \lim_{x \to 1} ⁡ \dfrac{f ( x )}{x\left|f ( f\left(x\right) )\right|}$ [ As the limit is in the form of 0/0]
$= \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2}}{\left|f\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\right|} = \dfrac{1}{14}$
$⇒ \left|f\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\right| = 7$
$⇒ f\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = 7asf\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$ can not be negative

26048.text: Paragraph: When a particle is restricted to move along $x$-axis between $x=0$ and $x=a$, where $a$ is of nanometer dimension, its energy can take only certain specific values. The allowed energies of the particle moving in such a restricted region, correspond to the formation of standing waves with nodes at its ends $x=0$ and $x=a$. The wavelength of this standing wave is related to the liner momentum $p$ of the particle according to the de Broglie relation. The energy of the particle of mass $m$ is related to its linear momentum as $E=\frac{p^2}{2 m}$. Thus, the energy of the particle can be denoted by a quantum number $n$ taking values $1,2,3, \ldots(n=1$, called the ground state) corresponding to the number of loops in the standing wave. Use the model described above to answer the following three questions for a particle moving in the line $x=0$ to $x=a$ [Take $h=6.6 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{Js}$ and $e=1.6 \times 10^{-19} \mathrm{C}$ ]Question: The speed of the particle that can take discrete values is proportional to

26796.subject: Physics
26796.text:
A particle of unit mass is moving along the x-axis under the influence of a force and its total energy is conserved. Four possible forms of the potential energy of the particle are given in column I (a and ${U}_{0}$ are constants). Match the potential energies in column I to the corresponding statement(s) in column II.
Column I Column II
A. ${U}_{1}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{{U}_{0}}{2}{\left[1 - {\left(\dfrac{x}{a}\right)}^{2}\right]}^{2}$ P. The force acting on the particle is zero at $x = a$
B. ${U}_{2}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{{U}_{0}}{2}{\left(\dfrac{x}{a}\right)}^{2}$ Q. The force acting on the particle is zero at $x = 0$ .
C. ${U}_{3}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{{U}_{0}}{2}{\left(\dfrac{x}{a}\right)}^{2}exp ⁡ \left[- {\left(\dfrac{x}{a}\right)}^{2}\right]$ R. The force acting on the particle is zero at $x = - a$
D. ${U}_{4}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{{U}_{0}}{2}\left[\dfrac{x}{a} - \dfrac{1}{3}{\left(\dfrac{x}{a}\right)}^{3}\right]$ S. The particle experiences an attractive force towards $x = 0$ in the region $\left|x\right| < a$
T. The particle with total energy $\dfrac{{U}_{0}}{4}$ can oscillate about the point $x = - a$
26796.sol:
${U}_{1}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{{U}_{0}}{2}{\left[1 - \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}\right]}^{2}$
$F = - \dfrac{{U}_{0}}{2}2\left[1 - \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}\right]\left[- \dfrac{2x}{{a}^{2}}\right]$
$= \dfrac{2{U}_{0}}{{a}^{4}}\left[{a}^{2} - {x}^{2}\right]x$
$F = \dfrac{2{U}_{0}}{{a}^{4}}x\left(a - x\right)\left(a + x\right)$
$F = 0$ , at $x = 0, a, - a$
$\left\begin{array}{ll}x = - a, U = 0, \\ x = 0, U = \dfrac{{U}_{0}}{2}\end{array}\right\} ⇒$ Oscillate when total ME is less then $\dfrac{{U}_{0}}{2}$
$A \to P, Q, R, T$
B- ${U}_{0}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{{U}_{0}}{2}{\left(\dfrac{x}{a}\right)}^{2}$
$F = - \dfrac{{U}_{0}x}{{a}^{2}}$
$F = 0, x = 0$
$B \to Q, S$
C- ${U}_{3}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{{U}_{0}}{2}\left[{\left(\dfrac{x}{a}\right)}^{2}exp ⁡ \left(- \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}\right)\right]$
$F = - \dfrac{{U}_{0}}{2}\left[\dfrac{2x}{{a}^{2}}exp ⁡ \left(- \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}\right) + \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}exp ⁡ \left(- \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}\right)\left(- \dfrac{2x}{{a}^{2}}\right)\right]$
$= - \dfrac{{U}_{0}}{2}\dfrac{2x}{{a}^{4}}exp ⁡ \left(- \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}\right)\left[{a}^{2} - {x}^{2}\right]$
$= \dfrac{{U}_{0}}{{a}^{4}}{e}^{\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}}\left[x\left(x + a\right)\left(x - a\right)\right]$
$x = 0, x = - a, x = + a, F = 0$
$x = 0, U = 0$ even function hence minima
$C \to P, Q, R, S$
D- ${U}_{4}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{{U}_{0}}{2}\left[\dfrac{x}{a} - \dfrac{{x}^{3}}{3{a}^{3}}\right]$
$F = - \dfrac{{U}_{0}}{a}\left[\dfrac{1}{a} - \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{3}}\right] = \dfrac{{U}_{0}}{2{a}^{3}}\left[{x}^{2} - {a}^{2}\right]$
$x = + a, x = - a, F = 0$
$x = - a, U = - \dfrac{{U}_{0}}{3}, x = + a, U = + \dfrac{{U}_{0}}{3}$
Hence oscillate about $x = - a$ if $T . M . E < \dfrac{{U}_{0}}{3}$
$D \to P, R, T$

27492.text: In a linear tetrapeptide (Constituted with different amino acids), (number of amino acids) - (number of peptide bonds) is
27492.sol:
A tetrapeptide is a peptide, classified as an oligopeptide, since it only consists of four amino acids joined by peptide bonds.

A peptide bond, also referred to as an amide bond, is formed between the α-nitrogen atom of one amino acid and the carbonyl carbon of a second.

Example of tetrapeptide is: $Tuftsin\left\{( L - threonyl ) - ( L - lysyl ) - ( L - prolyl ) - ( L - arginine )\right\}$is a peptide related primarily to the immune system function

As we can see in this example

No. of Amino Acids $= 4$

No. of Peptide bonds $= 3$

Hence, (number of amino acids) - (number of peptide bonds) $= 1$

28176.text: Consider a complex reaction taking place in three steps with rate constants $k_1, k_2$ and $k_3$ respectively. The overall rate constant $k$ is given by the expression $k=\sqrt{\frac{k_1 k_3}{k_2}}$. If the activation energies of the three steps are 60,30 and $10 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}{ }^{-1}$ respectively, then the overall energy of activation in $\mathrm{kJ} \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ is $\ldots\ldots$ . (Nearest integer)
28176.sol:
$\mathrm{k}_1, \mathrm{k}_2$ and $\mathrm{k}_3$ are given as rate constants of three steps of a complex reaction. Rate constant (k) of the overall reaction is given as
$k=\sqrt{\frac{k_1 k_3}{k_2}}$
Activation energies of the three steps are given as
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{a}_1}=60 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}, \mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{a}_2}=30 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}, \\
& \mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{a}_3}=10 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}
\end{aligned}$
From Arrhenius equation, we know that
$\mathrm{k}=\mathrm{Ae}^{-\mathrm{Ea} / \mathrm{RT} T}$
If $E_a$ is the activation energy of the overall reaction, then
$\begin{aligned}
& E_a=\frac{1}{2}\left[E_{a_1}+E_{a_3}-E_{a_2}\right] \\
& =\frac{1}{2}[60+10-30]=20 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}
\end{aligned}$

29124.subject: Chemistry
29124.text: In ammonium$-$phosphomolybdate, the oxidation state of $Mo$ is $+ _______$
29124.sol:
Phosphomolybdate is an anion containing both phosphorus and molybdenum, with the chemical formula ${\left({NH}_{4}\right)}_{3}{PO}_{4} \cdot 12{MoO}_{3}$.

The ammonium ion has a total charge of $+ 3$, and the phosphate ion has a total charge of $- 3$. Therefore, the $12{MoO}_{3}$ units in the compound must have a total charge of $+ 3 - ( - 3 ) = + 6$.

Each ${MoO}_{3}$ unit contains one $Mo$ atom and three $O$ atoms. The total oxidation state of the three $O$ atoms is $- 6$, since each $O$ atom has an oxidation state of $- 2$.

So,

$Mo + ( - 6 ) = 0Mo = + 6$

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
30082.sol:
For line II $∆ S$ is more negative than line I. In the Ellingham diagram, a sharp change in slope of the line is observed for $Mg - MgO$ at $~ {1120}^{o}C$ because that is the boiling point of magnesium.

From diagram, $∆ {S}_{I} = ( {S}_{solid} ) - ( {S}_{solid} + {S}_{gas} ) ∆ {S}_{II} = ( {S}_{liquid} ) - ( {S}_{solid} + {S}_{gas} )$

There is a large increase in entropy associated with the change of state of magnesium.

So, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

An aqueous solution of sodium or potassium salt of carboxylic acid is electrolysed in this reaction, resulting in the dissociation of the salt into a carboxylate ion and sodium or potassium ions. 

The total number of different alkanes are formed when the following mixture is subjected to electrolysis:

${CH}_{3}{COONa}_{\left(aq\right)}and{C}_{2}{H}_{5}{COONa}_{\left(aq\right)}$ 

In this ethane, butane and propane are formed.

${CH}_{3}COONa \to \overset{∙}{C}{H}_{3}$

${C}_{2}{H}_{5}COONa \to \overset{∙}{C}2{H}_{5}$

$2\overset{∙}{C}2{H}_{5} \to {CH}_{3} - {CH}_{2} - {CH}_{2} - {CH}_{3}$

$2C\overset{∙}{H}3 \to {CH}_{3} - {CH}_{3}$

$\overset{∙}{C}{H}_{3} + \overset{∙}{C}2{H}_{5} \to {CH}_{3} - {CH}_{2} - {CH}_{3}$

So, the total number of alkanes formed here will be $3$

$D$ Gatterman-Koch reaction $IV$ $CO, HCl, anhyd . {AlCl}_{3}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: $A \to III; B \to I; C \to II; D \to IV$
$A \to I; B \to II; C \to III; D \to IV$
$A \to III; B \to II; C \to I; D \to IV$
$A \to III; B \to I; C \to IV; D \to II$
31019.sol:
(A) Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reaction:

Carboxylic acid react with chlorine or bromine in the presence of phosphorus to give $\alpha -$halogenated carboxylic acids. The halogenation continues till all the hydrogen atom in the $\alpha -$position are replaced by halogen atoms. This reaction is called HVZ (Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky) reaction.

$\mathop{{CH}_{3}COOH}_{Aceticacid}\mathop{\to}_{- HCl}^{{Cl}_{2}, {P}_{4}}\mathop{{ClCH}_{2}COOH}_{Chloroaceticacid}\mathop{\to}_{- HCl}^{{Cl}_{2}, {P}_{4}}\mathop{{Cl}_{2}CHCOOH}_{Dichloroaceticacid}\mathop{\to}_{- HCl}^{{Cl}_{2}, {P}_{4}}\mathop{{Cl}_{3}CCOOH}_{Trichloroaceticacid}$

(B) Iodoform reaction:

The Iodoform reaction is a chemical reaction where a iodoform$\left({CHI}_{3}\right)$ is produced by the full iodonation of a methyl ketone (${RCOCH}_{3}$, where $R$ can be either a hydrogen atom, an alkyl or an aryl group) in the presence of a base.

$2NaOH + {I}_{2} \to NaOI + NaI{CH}_{3}{COCH}_{3} + 3NaOI \to {CH}_{3}COONa + {CHI}_{3} + 2NaOH$

(C) Etard reaction:

In Etard reaction, chromyl chloride oxidises methyl group to a chromium complex, which on hydrolysis gives corresponding Benzaldehyde. The equation for the reaction is:

${C}_{6}{H}_{5} - {CH}_{3} + {CrO}_{2}{Cl}_{2}\overset{{CS}_{2}}{\to}{C}_{6}{H}_{5} - CH\left({OCrOHCl}_{2}\right)\overset{{H}_{3}{O}^{+}}{\to}{C}_{6}{H}_{5} - CHO$

(D) Gatterman-Koch reaction

When benzene or its derivative is treated with carbon monoxide and hydrogen chloride in the presence of anhydrous aluminium chloride or cuprous chloride, it gives Benzaldehyde or substituted Benzaldehyde. The equation for the reaction is:

${C}_{6}{H}_{5} - {CH}_{3}\mathop{\to}_{Anh . {AlCl}_{3} / CuCl}^{CO + HCl}{C}_{6}{H}_{5} - CHO$

32222.subject: Chemistry
32222.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement-I: The orbitals having same energy are called as degenerate orbitals.
Statement-II: In hydrogen atom, $3p$ and $3d$ orbitals are not degenerate orbitals.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given
options: Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are true.
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are false
Statement-I is false but Statement-II is true
32222.sol:
Degenerate orbitals are the orbitals of the same subshell having equal energies. When the electrons of the orbitals are not influenced by any external factors like an electric field or magnetic field, they have same energies.

For a single electron species like hydrogen atom, the energy depends upon the principal quantum number $' n '$ only. Hence, $3s, 3pand3d$ oribitals have same energy. So, statement II is false.

Statement I is correct definition of degenerate orbitals.

Hence, the answer is option A.

33818.text: If the center and radius of the circle $\left|\dfrac{z - 2}{z - 3}\right| = 2$ are respectively $\left(\alpha, \beta\right)$ and $\gamma$, then $3\left(\alpha + \beta + \gamma\right) is equal to$
33818.sol:
Given:

$\left|\dfrac{z - 2}{z - 3}\right| = 2$

Let $z = x + iy$, then we have

$\left|\dfrac{x - 2 + iy}{x - 3 + iy}\right| = 2$

$⇒ \sqrt{{\left(x - 2\right)}^{2} + {y}^{2}} = 2\sqrt{{\left(x - 3\right)}^{2} + {y}^{2}}$

$⇒ {x}^{2} + {y}^{2} - 4x + 4 = 4{x}^{2} + 4{y}^{2} - 24x + 36$

$⇒ 3{x}^{2} + 3{y}^{2} - 20x + 32 = 0$

$⇒ {x}^{2} + {y}^{2} - \dfrac{20}{3}x + \dfrac{32}{3} = 0$

So, $\left(\alpha, \beta\right) ≡ \left(\dfrac{10}{3}, 0\right)$

And,

$\gamma = \sqrt{\dfrac{100}{9} - \dfrac{32}{3}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{4}{9}} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

Therefore,

$3\left(\alpha + \beta + \gamma\right) = 3\left(\dfrac{10}{3} + \dfrac{2}{3}\right) = 12$

Now, $( 2 ) + ( 3 )$

from $( 1 ) ,$ $P ( 1 ) = f ( 1 ) + g ( 1 ) = 0$

34235.text:
Let $f\left(x\right) = x + \dfrac{a}{{\pi}^{2} - 4}sinx + \dfrac{b}{{\pi}^{2} - 4}cosx$, $x \in \mathbb{R}$ be a function which satisfies $f\left(x\right) = x + {∫}_{0}^{\pi / 2}sin\left(x + y\right)f\left(y\right)dy$. Then $\left(a + b\right)$
is equal to
34235.sol:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = x + {∫}_{0}^{\pi / 2}sin\left(x + y\right)f\left(y\right)dy$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = x + {∫}_{0}^{\pi / 2}\left(sinxcosy + cosxsiny\right)f\left(y\right)dy$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = x + {∫}_{0}^{\pi / 2}\left(\left(cosyf\left(y\right)dy\right)sinx + \left(sinyf\left(y\right)dy\right)cosx\right)$

And,$f\left(x\right) = x + \dfrac{a}{{\pi}^{2} - 4}sinx + \dfrac{b}{{\pi}^{2} - 4}cosx, x \in \mathbb{R}$

On comparing both the equations of $f ( x )$ we get,

$⇒ \dfrac{a}{{\pi}^{2} - 4} = {∫}_{0}^{\pi / 2}cosyf\left(y\right)dy \ldots \left(1\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{b}{{\pi}^{2} - 4} = {∫}_{0}^{\pi / 2}sinyf\left(y\right)dy \ldots \left(2\right)$

Adding equation $\left(1\right)$ and equation $\left(2\right)$ we get,

$\dfrac{a + b}{{\pi}^{2} - 4} = {∫}_{0}^{\pi / 2}\left(siny + cosy\right)f\left(y\right)dy \ldots \left(3\right)$

$∵ {∫}_{0}^{a}f ( x ) d x = {∫}_{0}^{a}f ( a - x ) d x$

$∴ \dfrac{a + b}{{\pi}^{2} - 4} = {∫}_{0}^{\pi / 2}\left(siny + cosy\right)f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - y\right)dy \ldots \left(4\right)$

Add equation $\left(3\right)$ and equation $\left(4\right)$ we get,

$\dfrac{2\left(a + b\right)}{{\pi}^{2} - 4} = {∫}_{0}^{\pi / 2}\left(siny + cosy\right)\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} + \dfrac{\left(a + b\right)}{{\pi}^{2} - 4}\left(siny + cosy\right)\right)dy$

$⇒ \dfrac{2\left(a + b\right)}{{\pi}^{2} - 4} = \pi + \dfrac{a + b}{{\pi}^{2} - 4}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} + 1\right)$

$⇒ \left(a + b\right) = - 2\pi\left(\pi + 2\right)$

$⇒ 10 = \dfrac{16}{3} + c$

$⇒ c = \dfrac{14}{3}$

Now finding, $y = {e}^{9} - 2 ⇒ v = y + 2 = {e}^{9}$

Now putting the value in equation $\left(i\right)$ we get,

$⇒ u \cdot 3 = \dfrac{2}{3} \times 27 + \dfrac{14}{3} = 18 + \dfrac{14}{3}$

$⇒ x + 4 = u = 6 + \dfrac{14}{9}$

$⇒ x = 2 + \dfrac{14}{9} = \dfrac{32}{9}$

$∴ 1 \le {e}^{x} < 2$

$⇒ {\log}_{e}1 \le x < {\log}_{e}2$

$⇒ 0 \le x < {\log}_{e}2$

$⇒ x \in \left[0, {\log}_{e}2\right) .

$\begin{aligned}
& \text{ Sum$ of $odd terms }=\frac{4}{2}[2 \mathrm{a}+(4-1) 3]=24 \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{a}=\frac{3}{2} \\ & \text{ A.P. } \Rightarrow \frac{3}{2}, 3, \frac{9}{2}, 6, \frac{15}{2}, 9, \frac{21}{2}, 12
\end{aligned}$

38747.subject: Physics
38747.text: The figure given below shows an $LCR$ series circuit with two switches $S_1$ and $S_2$. When switch $S_1$ is closed keeping $S_2$ open, the phase difference $(\phi)$ between the current and source voltage is $30°$ and phase difference is $60°$ when $S_2$ is closed keeping $S_1$ open. The value of $(3L_1 - L_2)$ is _______ H.
38747.sol:
From the source $v = V_0 \sin(300t)$, the angular frequency is $\omega = 300\text{ rad/s}$.
Capacitance $C = 100\ \mu\text{F} = 10^{-4}\text{ F}$, so $X_C = \dfrac{1}{\omega C}$.

Case 1 ($S_1$ closed, $S_2$ open):
Closing $S_1$ short-circuits $L_2$, leaving an LCR series circuit with $C$, $R$ and $L_1$. With phase difference $\phi_1 = 30^\circ$:
$\tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{\omega L_1 - X_C}{R}$
$\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{\omega L_1 - X_C}{R} \Rightarrow R = \sqrt{3}\,(\omega L_1 - X_C)$ ... (1)

Case 2 ($S_2$ closed, $S_1$ open):
Closing $S_2$ short-circuits $L_1$, leaving an LCR series circuit with $C$, $R$ and $L_2$. With phase difference $\phi_2 = 60^\circ$:
$\tan 60^\circ = \dfrac{\omega L_2 - X_C}{R}$
$\sqrt{3} = \dfrac{\omega L_2 - X_C}{R} \Rightarrow \omega L_2 - X_C = R\sqrt{3}$ ... (2)

Substituting $R$ from (1) into (2):
$\omega L_2 - X_C = \sqrt{3}\,(\omega L_1 - X_C) \cdot \sqrt{3}$
$\omega L_2 - X_C = 3\omega L_1 - 3X_C$
$2X_C = 3\omega L_1 - \omega L_2 = \omega(3L_1 - L_2)$

Therefore:
$3L_1 - L_2 = \dfrac{2X_C}{\omega} = \dfrac{2}{\omega^2 C}$

Substituting $\omega = 300\text{ rad/s}$ and $C = 10^{-4}\text{ F}$:
$\omega^2 C = (300)^2 \cdot 10^{-4} = 9 \times 10^4 \cdot 10^{-4} = 9$

$3L_1 - L_2 = \dfrac{2}{9}\text{ H}$

Hence, the correct option is $(2)\ \dfrac{2}{9}$.

39175.subject: Physics
39175.text: Two metallic plates form a parallel plate capacitor. The distance between the plate is '$d$'. A metal sheet of thickness $\dfrac{d}{2}$ and of area equal to area of each plate is introduced between the plates. What will be the ratio of the new capacitance to the original capacitance of the capacitor?
39175.sol:
Before the metal sheet is inserted, capacitance is given by $C = \dfrac{{ε}_{0}A}{d}$.

After the sheet is inserted, the system is equivalent to two capacitors in series, each of capacitance ${C}^{'} = \dfrac{{ε}_{0}A}{\left(\dfrac{d}{4}\right)} = 4C$.
The equivalent capacity is now $\dfrac{1}{C '} = \dfrac{1}{4C} + \dfrac{1}{4C} ⇒ C ' = 2C$.

The ratio is $\dfrac{C}{C '} = \dfrac{1}{2} = 1: 2$

39202.subject: Physics
39202.text: A parallel plate capacitor has plate of length $l$, width $w$ and separation of plates is $d$. It is connected to a battery of emf $V$. A dielectric slab of the same thickness $d$ and of dielectric constant $K = 4$ is being inserted between the plates of the capacitor. At what length of the slab inside plates, will the energy stored in the capacitor be two times the initial energy stored?
39202.sol:
Given,

Length of plate of parallel plate capacitor is $l$

Width of plate is $w$

Separation of plates is $d$.

Emf of battery is $V$

Thickness of dielectric slab is $d$

Dielectric constant of slab is $K = 4$

Capacitance of capacitor before the insertion of dielectric slab is

${C}_{0} = \dfrac{A{ε}_{0}}{d} = \dfrac{wl{ε}_{0}}{d} . . . ( 1 )$

Energy stored in the capacitor before the insertion of dielectrics is given by,

${U}_{0} = \dfrac{1}{2}{C}_{0}{V}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{wl{ε}_{0}}{d}\right){V}^{2} . . . ( 2 )$

Suppose that, the slab is inside the plate at $y$ distance, therefore, it becomes the combination of two capacitors one with air with length $( l - y )$ and another with dielectric with length $y$ as shown in diagram.

Now the capacitance of capacitor in parallel combination is given by,

$C = {C}_{1} + {C}_{2} . . . ( 3 )$

Where,

${C}_{1} = \dfrac{w ( l - y ) {ε}_{0}}{d} . . . ( 4 )$

${C}_{1} = \dfrac{wyK{ε}_{0}}{d} . . . ( 5 )$

Now energy stored in this combination of capacitor is given by

$U = \dfrac{1}{2} ( {C}_{1} + {C}_{2} ) {V}^{2} . . . ( 6 )$

Now according to the given condition,

$2{U}_{0} = U$

$⇒ 2\left(\dfrac{1}{2}{C}_{0}{V}^{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\left({C}_{1} + {C}_{2}\right){V}^{2}$

$⇒ 2{C}_{0} = {C}_{1} + {C}_{2}$

$⇒ 2\left(\dfrac{{ϵ}_{0}wl}{d}\right) = \dfrac{{ϵ}_{0}Kwy}{d} + \dfrac{{ϵ}_{0}w ( l - y )}{d}$

$⇒ 2l = Ky + l - y$

$⇒ l = 4y - y = 3y$

$⇒ y = \dfrac{l}{3}$

41483.text: A long straight wire of circular cross-section (radius $a$) is carrying steady current $I .$ The current $I$ is uniformly distributed across this cross-section. The magnetic field is
options: inversely proportional to $r$ in the region $r < a$ and uniform throughout in the region $r > a$
directly proportional to $r$ in the region $r < a$ and inversely proportional to $r$ in the region $r > a$
Zero in the region $r < a$ and inversely proportional to $r$ in the region $r > a$
uniform in the region $r < a$ and inversely proportional to distance $r$ from the axis, in the region $r > a$
41483.sol:
The formula to calculate the magnetic field inside the conducting wire is given by

${B}_{\text{in}} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}Jr}{2} . . . ( 1 )$

The formula to calculate the magnetic field outside the conducting wire is given by

${B}_{\text{out}} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}J{a}^{2}}{2r} . . . ( 2 )$

From equation (1), it can be concluded that the magnetic field is directly proportional to the radial distance inside the wire, whereas from equation (2), it can be concluded that the magnetic field is inversely proportional to the radial distance outside the wire.

41502.text:
Match List I with List II

List – I
(Current configuration)		 List – II
(Magnetic field at point $O$)
A I. ${B}_{0} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I}{4\pir} [ \pi + 2 ]$
B II. ${B}_{0} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{4}\dfrac{I}{r}$
C III. ${B}_{0} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I}{2\pir} [ \pi - 1 ]$
D IV. ${B}_{0} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I}{4\pir} [ \pi + 1 ]$

Choose the correct answer from the option given below:
41502.sol:
(A)

Here net magnetic field will be sum of magnetic field due to straight wires $ab, de$ and due to loop $bcd$.

So, ${B}_{ab} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} = {B}_{de}$ (directed out of the plane in both cases)

${B}_{bcd} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} ( 2\pi )$ (in the plane)

Thus, magnetic field at $O$ is

${B}_{O} = - \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} + \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} ( 2\pi ) - \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r}$

${B}_{O} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{2\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} ( \pi - 1 )$ (III)

(B)

Here net magnetic field will be sum of magnetic field due to straight wires $ab, de$ and semicircular arc $bcd$.

${B}_{ab} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} = {B}_{de}$ (directed out of the plane in both cases)

${B}_{bcd} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} ( \pi )$ (out of the plane)

Thus, net magnetic field at $O$ is

${B}_{O} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} + \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} ( \pi ) + \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r}$

${B}_{0} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} ( \pi + 2 )$ (I)

(C)

Here net magnetic field will be sum of magnetic field due to straight wires $ab, de$ and due to loop $bcd$.

${B}_{ab} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r}$ (directed in the plane)

${B}_{bcd} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} ( \pi )$ (in the plane)

${B}_{de} = 0$ (passing through the axis)

Thus, magnetic field at $O$ is

${B}_{O} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} ( \pi + 1 )$ (IV)

(D)

Here net magnetic field will be sum of magnetic field due to straight wires $ab, de$ and due to loop $bcd$.

${B}_{ab} = 0 = {B}_{de}$ (passing through the axis)

${B}_{bcd} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{4\pi}\dfrac{I}{r} ( \pi )$ (out of the plane)

Thus, magnetic field at $O$ is

${B}_{O} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}I}{4r}$ (II).

A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

real, formed at $7\text{ cm}$ right of lens $Q$, with a size smaller than that of $AB$
42852.sol:
For lens $P$:

$\dfrac{1}{v_1} - \dfrac{1}{u_1} = \dfrac{1}{f_1}$

$\dfrac{1}{v_1} - \dfrac{1}{-15} = \dfrac{1}{10}$

$\dfrac{1}{v_1} = \dfrac{1}{10} - \dfrac{1}{15} = \dfrac{1}{30} \Rightarrow v_1 = 30\text{ cm}$

Magnification $m_1 = \dfrac{v_1}{u_1} = \dfrac{30}{-15} = -2$

The image formed by lens $P$ acts as a virtual object for lens $Q$. Since the distance between the lenses is $15\text{ cm}$, the object distance for lens $Q$ is:

$u_2 = 30 - 15 = +15\text{ cm}$

For lens $Q$:

$\dfrac{1}{v_2} - \dfrac{1}{u_2} = \dfrac{1}{f_2}$

$\dfrac{1}{v_2} - \dfrac{1}{15} = \dfrac{1}{15}$

$\dfrac{1}{v_2} = \dfrac{2}{15} \Rightarrow v_2 = 7.5\text{ cm}$

The positive sign indicates that the final image is real and formed $7.5\text{ cm}$ to the right of lens $Q$.

Magnification $m_2 = \dfrac{v_2}{u_2} = \dfrac{7.5}{15} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Total magnification $m = m_1 \times m_2 = -2 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = -1$

Since $|m| = 1$, the size of the final image is the same as that of the object $AB$.

Answer: real, formed at $7.5\text{ cm}$ right of lens $Q$, with a size same as that of $AB$

43231.text: A ring and a solid sphere rotating about an axis passing through their centres have same radii of gyration. The axis of rotation is perpendicular to plane of ring. The ratio of radius of ring to that of sphere is $\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{x}}$. The value of $x$ is _____.
43231.sol:
The moment of inertia of the ring about an axis perpendicular to the plane of ring is ${I}_{r} = m{k}^{2}$.

The moment of inertia of the sphere is

${I}_{s} = \dfrac{2}{5}m{R}^{2}s$

It is given that

$m{k}^{2} = m{R}^{2}r = \dfrac{2}{5}m{{R}_{s}}^{2} . . . ( i )$

From equation (i)

${R}_{r} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{5}}{R}_{s}$

From the question, it can be written that

$\dfrac{{R}_{r}}{{R}_{s}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{x}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{R}_{r}}{{R}_{s}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{5}} ⇒ x = 5$

44198.subject: Physics
44198.text: In a Young's double slit experiment, the intensity at some point on the screen is found to be $\dfrac{3}{4}$ times of the maximum of the interference pattern. The path difference between the interfering waves at this point is $\dfrac{\lambda}{x}$ where $\lambda$ is wavelength of the incident light. The value of $x$ is _______.
44198.sol:
The intensity at a point in Young's double slit experiment is given by $I = I_{max} \cos^2\left(\dfrac{\phi}{2}\right)$

Given $I = \dfrac{3}{4} I_{max}$

$\dfrac{3}{4} I_{max} = I_{max} \cos^2\left(\dfrac{\phi}{2}\right)$

$\cos\left(\dfrac{\phi}{2}\right) = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

$\dfrac{\phi}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$

$\phi = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$

The phase difference $\phi$ is related to the path difference $\Delta x$ by $\phi = \dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda} \Delta x$

$\dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda} \Delta x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$

$\Delta x = \dfrac{\lambda}{6}$

Comparing with $\Delta x = \dfrac{\lambda}{x}$, we get $x = 6$

Answer: $6$

46225.text: Figure shows three spherical and equipotential surfaces $A, B$ and $C$ round a point charge $q$. The potential difference $V_A-V_B=V_B-V_C$. If $t_1$ and $t_2$ be the distances between them, then
46225.sol:
Potential difference between two equipotential surfaces $A$ and $B$,
$V_A-V_B=k q\left(\frac{1}{r_A}-\frac{1}{r_B}\right)=k q\left(\frac{r_B-r_A}{r_A r_B}\right)=\frac{k q t_1}{r_A r_B}$
or $\quad t_1=\frac{\left(V_A-V_B\right) r_A r_B}{k q}$
or
$t_1 \propto r_A r_B$
Similarly, $t_2 \propto r_B r_C$
Since, $r_A \lt r_B \lt r_C$, therefore, $r_A r_B \lt r_B r_C$
$\therefore \quad t_1 \lt t_2$

Rate of radiated energy $\left(E_1\right)=17 \mathrm{~W}$
Final temperature $\left(T_2\right)=273^{\circ} \mathrm{C}=273+273=546 \mathrm{~K}$
We know, from the Stefan's law, $E \propto T^4 \begin{aligned} & \text{ or } \quad \frac{E_1}{E_2}=\left(\frac{T_1}{T_2}\right)^4=\left(\frac{418}{546}\right)^4 \\ & \therefore \quad \frac{E_1}{E_2}=0.343 \\ & \end{aligned}$
Therefore, final radiated energy, $E_2=\frac{E_1}{0.343}=\frac{17}{0.343}=49.6 \mathrm{~W}$

54876.subject: Chemistry
54876.text: Which from following compounds has lowest boiling point?
54876.sol:
The boiling point of alcohols is influenced by hydrogen bonding and London dispersion forces, both present in these compounds.

Hydrogen bonding occurs through the hydroxyl group, contributing significantly to boiling points. London dispersion forces increase with molecular size and surface area, strengthening with additional carbon atoms.

Methanol ($\mathrm{CH_3 OH}$) possesses only one carbon atom, resulting in the weakest London dispersion forces among the alcohols. While hydrogen bonding is present, the reduced molecular size leads to lower overall intermolecular attraction.

$\text{Less energy is required to overcome these weaker forces, resulting in methanol's lower boiling point.}$

The correct answer is D.

55256.text: Identify the major product obtained when ethyl amine is reacted with excess of methyl iodide ?
55256.sol:
Ethyl amine reacts with excess of methyl iodide to undergo exhaustive methylation, forming a quaternary ammonium salt.

$C_2H_5NH_2 + CH_3I \rightarrow C_2H_5NHCH_3 + HI$

$C_2H_5NHCH_3 + CH_3I \rightarrow C_2H_5N(CH_3)_2 + HI$

$C_2H_5N(CH_3)_2 + CH_3I \rightarrow [C_2H_5N(CH_3)_3]^+ I^-$

Since methyl iodide is in excess, the reaction does not stop at the secondary or tertiary amine stage but proceeds to the final quaternary ammonium salt.

The major product obtained is ethyltrimethylammonium iodide.

Answer: Ethyltrimethylammonium iodide

58865.text:
Calculate the number of atoms present per unit cell if product of density and volume of unit cell is $1.8 \times 10^{-22} \mathrm{ g}$
[Mass of an atom $=4.5 \times 10^{-23} \mathrm{ g}$]
58865.sol:
The density $\rho$ of a unit cell relates atomic parameters through $\rho V = Z m$, where $V$ is volume, $Z$ is atomic count per unit cell, and $m$ is atomic mass.

Given $\rho V = 1.8 \times 10^{-22}$ g and $m = 4.5 \times 10^{-23}$ g, we substitute into the relation:

$1.8 \times 10^{-22} = Z \times (4.5 \times 10^{-23})$

Solving for $Z$:

$Z = \frac{1.8 \times 10^{-22}}{4.5 \times 10^{-23}} = \frac{1.8}{4.5} \times 10^{1} = 0.4 \times 10 = 4$

The unit cell contains 4 atoms, corresponding to choice $\boxed{C}$.

59152.subject: Chemistry
59152.text: Calculate the relative lowering of vapour pressure of solution containing 3 g urea in 50 g water. [ molar mass of urea $=60 \mathrm{ g} \mathrm{ mol}^{-1}$ ]
59152.sol:
Using Raoult's law, the relative lowering of vapor pressure equals the mole fraction of solute: $\frac{\Delta P}{P^0} = X_{\text{urea}}$.

Given 3 g urea (molar mass 60 g mol^{-1}$) and 50 g water (molar mass 18 g mol^{-1}$), the moles are:

$n_{\text{urea}} = \frac{3}{60} = 0.05$ mol

$n_{\text{water}} = \frac{50}{18} \approx 2.7778$ mol

The mole fraction of urea is:

$X_{\text{urea}} = \frac{0.05}{0.05 + 2.7778} = \frac{0.05}{2.8278} \approx 0.01768$

Rounding to three decimal places gives $\frac{\Delta P}{P^0} \approx 0.018$, which corresponds to option C.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{C}}$

60204.sol:
Given $f(x) = \int \dfrac{x+3}{x^2-9x+20}\,dx$

Differentiating with respect to $x$, we get:

$f'(x) = \dfrac{x+3}{x^2-9x+20} = \dfrac{x+3}{(x-4)(x-5)}$

For $f(x)$ to be decreasing, $f'(x) \le 0$.

$\dfrac{x+3}{(x-4)(x-5)} \le 0$

The critical points are $x = -3$, $x = 4$, and $x = 5$.

Using the wavy curve method to determine the sign of $f'(x)$ in different intervals:

For $x \in (5, \infty)$, $f'(x) > 0$

For $x \in (4, 5)$, $f'(x) < 0$

For $x \in (-3, 4)$, $f'(x) > 0$

For $x \in (-\infty, -3)$, $f'(x) < 0$

Therefore, $f'(x) \le 0$ for $x \in (-\infty, -3] \cup (4, 5)$.

Hence, $f(x)$ decreases on $(-\infty, -3] \cup (4, 5)$.

Answer: decreases on $(-\infty, -3] \cup (4, 5)$

61148.sol:
A coin is tossed 4 times \therefore $\mathrm{n}(\mathrm{S})=2^4=16 Following possibilities exist.
(i) All Heads $\Rightarrow 1$ way
(ii) 3 Heads, 1 Tail ⇒ \frac{4 !}{3 !}=4$ ways
(iii) 2 Heads, 2 Tails $\Rightarrow \frac{4 !}{2 ! 2 !}=6$ ways
(iv) 1 Head, 3 Tails $\Rightarrow \frac{4 !}{3 !}=4$ ways
(v) 0 head, 4 Tails $\Rightarrow 1$ way
$\therefore$ Required probability. $\begin{aligned} \text{$ and $} =\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{x}=0,1,2)=\frac{1}{16}+\frac{4}{16}+\frac{6}{16}$\\
& =$\frac{11}{16}
\end{aligned}$

61360.subject: Mathematics
61360.text: The order and degree of differential equation of all tangent lines to the parabola $x^2=4 \mathrm{y}$ is respectively.
61360.sol:
Differential equation of tangent lines to the parabola $x^2 = 4y$.

The general equation of a tangent line to $x^2 = 4y$ with slope $m$ is $y = mx - m^2$.

Differentiating with respect to $x$ gives $\frac{dy}{dx} = m$. Substituting $m = \frac{dy}{dx}$ into the tangent equation yields $y = x\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right) - \left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^2$.

Rewriting the differential equation as $\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 - x\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right) + y = 0$ shows the highest derivative is $\frac{dy}{dx}$, which is first order. The power of this derivative is 2, so the degree is 2.

The order is 1 and the degree is 2.

& \quad \text{ at } x=4, \cos \theta=\frac{4}{5}, \sin \theta=\frac{3}{5} \text{$ and $} y=3 \\

62719.text: Define $\mathrm{f}(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{cl}\mathrm{b}-\mathrm{a} x & , \text{ if } x < 2 \\ 3 & , \text{ if } x=2 \\ \mathrm{a}+2 \mathrm{ b} x & , \text{ if } x > 2\end{array}\right.$ and if $\lim _{x \rightarrow 2} \mathrm{f}(x)$ exists, then $\frac{\mathrm{a}}{\mathrm{b}}=$
62719.sol:
The limit $\lim_{x \to 2} f(x)$ exists if and only if the left-hand and right-hand limits at $x = 2$ are equal.

For $x < 2$, $f(x) = b - a x$, so the left-hand limit is $\lim_{x \to 2^-} f(x) = b - 2a$.

For $x > 2$, $f(x) = a + 2b x$, giving the right-hand limit $\lim_{x \to 2^+} f(x) = a + 4b$.

Setting these equal: $b - 2a = a + 4b$.

This simplifies to $-3b = 3a$, and dividing both sides by $3b$ (since $b \neq 0$ for the ratio to be defined) yields $\frac{a}{b} = -1$.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{B}}$

64481.text: If the shortest distance between the lines $\frac{x-\mathrm{k}}{2}=\frac{\mathrm{y}-4}{3}=\frac{\mathrm{z}-3}{4}$ and $\frac{x-2}{4}=\frac{\mathrm{y}-4}{6}=\frac{\mathrm{z}-7}{8}$ is $\frac{13}{\sqrt{29}}$, then $\mathrm{k}=$
options: $-\left(\cos x-\frac{2}{3} \cos ^2 x+\frac{\cos ^5 x}{5}+c\right)$, where $c$ is the constant of integration
$\left(\cos x-\frac{2}{3} \cos ^2 x+\frac{\cos ^5 x}{5}\right)+\mathrm{c}$, where c is the constant of integration
64481.sol:
The line $L_1: \frac{x-k}{2} = \frac{y-4}{3} = \frac{z-3}{4}$ passes through $A(k, 4, 3)$ with direction vector $\vec{d_1} = 2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}$. The line $L_2: \frac{x-2}{4} = \frac{y-4}{6} = \frac{z-7}{8}$ passes through $B(2, 4, 7)$ with direction vector $\vec{d_2} = 4\hat{i} + 6\hat{j} + 8\hat{k}$.

Observe that $\vec{d_2} = 2\vec{d_1}$, so the lines are parallel. The vector connecting points $A$ and $B$ is $\vec{AB} = (2-k)\hat{i} + 0\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}$.

The shortest distance between parallel lines is given by $D = \frac{|\vec{AB} \times \vec{d_1}|}{|\vec{d_1}|}$ where $|\vec{d_1}| = \sqrt{29}$.

The cross product yields $\vec{AB} \times \vec{d_1} = -12\hat{i} + 4k\hat{j} + (6-3k)\hat{k}$, with magnitude $|\vec{AB} \times \vec{d_1}| = \sqrt{25k^2 - 36k + 180}$.

Given $D = \frac{13}{\sqrt{29}}$, equate:

$\frac{\sqrt{25k^2 - 36k + 180}}{\sqrt{29}} = \frac{13}{\sqrt{29}}$

Square both sides: $25k^2 - 36k + 180 = 169$

Simplify to: $25k^2 - 36k + 11 = 0$

Factor: $(k - 1)(25k - 11) = 0$

Thus $k = 1$ or $k = \frac{11}{25}$.

The value $k = 1$ corresponds to option A.

65119.text: A vector $\bar{r}$ of magnitude $3\sqrt{2}$ units which makes angles of $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ and $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ respectively with Y and Z axes is
65119.sol:
Let the direction cosines of the vector $\bar{r}$ be $l, m, n$.

Given that the vector makes angles of $\dfrac{\pi}{4} and \dfrac{\pi}{2}$ with the Y and Z axes respectively, we have:
$m = \cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$
$n = \cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = 0$

Using the relation $l^2 + m^2 + n^2 = 1$:
$l^2 + \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2 + 0^2 = 1$
$l^2 + \dfrac{1}{2} = 1$
$l^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} \Rightarrow l = \pm \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

The vector $\bar{r}$ is given by:
$\bar{r} = |\bar{r}|(l\hat{i} + m\hat{j} + n\hat{k})$

Substituting the given magnitude $|\bar{r}| = 3\sqrt{2}$ and the direction cosines:
$\bar{r} = 3\sqrt{2} \left(\pm \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\hat{i} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\hat{j} +0\hat{k}\right)$
\bar{r} = \pm3\hat{i} + 3\hat{j}$

Answer: $\bar{r} = \pm3\hat{i} + 3\hat{j}$$

65156.text: If $\overline{\mathrm{b}}$ and $\overline{\mathrm{c}}$ are unit vectors and $|\bar{a}|=7$, $\bar{a} \times(\bar{b} \times \bar{c})+\bar{b} \times(\bar{c} \times \bar{a})=\frac{1}{2} \bar{a}$, then angle between the vectors $\bar{a}$ and $\overline{\mathrm{c}}$ and angle between the vectors $\overline{\mathrm{b}}$ and $\overline{\mathrm{c}}$ are respectively.
65156.sol:
Given: $\bar{a} \times (\bar{b} \times \bar{c}) + \bar{b} \times (\bar{c} \times \bar{a}) = \frac{1}{2} \bar{a}$, $|\bar{a}| = 7$, and $\bar{b}$, $\bar{c}$ are unit vectors.

Using the vector triple product identity $\bar{x} \times (\bar{y} \times \bar{z}) = (\bar{x} \cdot \bar{z})\bar{y} - (\bar{x} \cdot \bar{y})\bar{z}$:

$\bar{a} \times (\bar{b} \times \bar{c}) = (\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})\bar{b} - (\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b})\bar{c}$

$\bar{b} \times (\bar{c} \times \bar{a}) = (\bar{b} \cdot \bar{a})\bar{c} - (\bar{b} \cdot \bar{c})\bar{a}$

Substituting into the original equation:

$(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})\bar{b} - (\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b})\bar{c} + (\bar{b} \cdot \bar{a})\bar{c} - (\bar{b} \cdot \bar{c})\bar{a} = \frac{1}{2} \bar{a}$

Noting $\bar{a} \cdot \bar{b} = \bar{b} \cdot \bar{a}$, the $\bar{c}$ terms cancel:

$(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})\bar{b} - (\bar{b} \cdot \bar{c})\bar{a} = \frac{1}{2} \bar{a}$

Rearranging:

$(\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c})\bar{b} = \left(\frac{1}{2} + \bar{b} \cdot \bar{c}\right)\bar{a}$

Since $\bar{a}$ and $\bar{b}$ are generally non-parallel, both coefficients must be zero:

$\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c} = 0$ and $\frac{1}{2} + \bar{b} \cdot \bar{c} = 0$

Thus, $\bar{a} \cdot \bar{c} = 0 \Rightarrow$ angle is $90^{}^{\circ}$

$\bar{b} \cdot \bar{c} = -\frac{1}{2} = \cos\theta_{bc} \Rightarrow \theta_{bc} = 120^{}^{\circ}$

Matching with the options, the correct choice is C.

65171.sol:
Given vectors $\bar{a}=2 \hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ and $\bar{b}=\hat{i}+2 \hat{j}-\hat{k}$, find vector $\bar{c} = x \hat{i} + y \hat{j} + z \hat{k}$ that is coplanar with $\bar{a}$ and $\bar{b}$ and perpendicular to $\bar{a}$.

Coplanarity requires $\bar{c} \cdot (\bar{a} \times \bar{b}) = 0$. Compute $\bar{a} \times \bar{b} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} \text{ and } \hat{j} \text{ and } \hat{k} \\ 2 \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } 1 \\ 1 \text{ and } 2 \text{ and } -1 \end{vmatrix} = \hat{i}(-1 - 2) - \hat{j}(-2 - 1) + \hat{k}(4 - 1) = -3\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$.

Dot product gives $-3x + 3y + 3z = 0$; dividing by 3 yields $-x + y + z = 0$.

Perpendicularity requires $\bar{c} \cdot \bar{a} = 0$, giving $2x + y + z = 0$.

Subtracting the first equation from the second: $(2x + y + z) - (-x + y + z) = 0 \implies 3x = 0 \implies x = 0$.

Substitute $x = 0$ into $-x + y + z = 0$ to get $y + z = 0$, so $z = -y$.

Thus, $\bar{c} = y(\hat{j} - \hat{k})$. Comparing with the options, $\boxed{\text{D}}$ gives $-\hat{j} + \hat{k} = -1(\hat{j} - \hat{k})$, which matches the form with $y = -1$.

65861.text: In Bohr's atomic model, the energy of the electron is 'E' in the second orbit of hydrogen atom. So the energy of the electron in the third orbit of helium atom $(Z = 2)$ will be
65861.sol:
The energy of an electron in the $n$-th orbit of a hydrogen-like atom is given by $E_n \propto \dfrac{Z^2}{n^2}$.

For the second orbit of a hydrogen atom ($Z=1, n=2$):

$E = k \dfrac{1^2}{2^2} = \dfrac{k}{4} \Rightarrow k = 4E$

For the third orbit of a helium atom ($Z=2, n=3$):

$E' = k \dfrac{2^2}{3^2} = k \dfrac{4}{9}$

Substituting $k = 4E$:

$E' = 4E \times \dfrac{4}{9} = \dfrac{16E}{9}$

Answer: $\dfrac{16\,E}{9}$

66074.text: A parallel plate capacitor has plate area $50 \mathrm{ cm}^2$ and plate separation 3 mm. The space between the plates is filled with a dielectric medium of thickness 1 mm and dielectric constant 4. The capacitance becomes (\epsilon_0=$ permittivity of free space)$
66074.sol:
The capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor with a dielectric slab of thickness t and dielectric constant K inserted between plates separated by distance d is given by:

$C = \frac{\epsilon_0 A}{d - t + \frac{t}{K}}$

Substituting the given values $A = 50 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{m^2}$, $d = 3 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{m}$, $t = 1 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{m}$, and $K = 4$:

$C = \frac{\epsilon_0 (50 \times 10^{-4})}{(3 \times 10^{-3}) - (1 \times 10^{-3}) + \frac{(1 \times 10^{-3})}{4}}$

Evaluating the denominator:

$d - t = 2 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{m}$

$\frac{t}{K} = 0.25 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{m}$

Total denominator $= 2.25 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{m}$

The capacitance simplifies to:

$C = \frac{50 \times 10^{-4}}{2.25 \times 10^{-3}} \epsilon_0 = \frac{5}{2.25} \epsilon_0 = \frac{20}{9} \epsilon_0$

This result corresponds to option B.

67646.subject: Physics
67646.text: Two wires of same length are bent to form the circular loop with two turns and a square loop of one turn. Both of them carry same current. The ratio of magnetic moment of circular loop of two turns to that of square loop is
67646.sol:
Let the length of the wire be $L$ and the current be $I$.

For the circular loop with two turns, the total length is $2 \times 2\pi r = L$, which gives $r = \dfrac{L}{4\pi}$.

The magnetic moment of the circular loop is $M_1 = N_1 I A_1 = 2 I (\pi r^2) = 2 I \pi \left(\dfrac{L}{4\pi}\right)^2 = \dfrac{I L^2}{8\pi}$.

For the square loop with one turn, the perimeter is $4a = L$, which gives $a = \dfrac{L}{4}$.

The magnetic moment of the square loop is $M_2 = N_2 I A_2 = 1 I a^2 = I \left(\dfrac{L}{4}\right)^2 = \dfrac{I L^2}{16}$.

The ratio of their magnetic moments is $\dfrac{M_1}{M_2} = \dfrac{\dfrac{I L^2}{8\pi}}{\dfrac{I L^2}{16}} = \dfrac{16}{8\pi} = \dfrac{2}{\pi}$.

Answer: $2 : \pi$

68134.text:
A spherical ball of radius $1$ mm and density $10.5$ g/cc is dropped in glycerine of coefficient of viscosity $9.8$ poise and density $1.5$ g/cc. Viscous force on the ball when it attains constant velocity is $3696 \times 10^{-x}$ N. The value of $x$ is
(Given, $g = 9.8 \text{ m}/\text{s}^2$ and $\pi = \dfrac{22}{7}$)
68134.sol:
When the spherical ball attains constant (terminal) velocity, the net force acting on it is zero. The downward weight of the ball is balanced by the upward buoyant force and the viscous force.

Viscous force $F_v = W - F_B$

$F_v = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3 \rho g - \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3 \sigma g$

$F_v = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3 (\rho - \sigma) g$

Given values in SI units:
$r = 1 \text{ mm} = 10^{-3} \text{ m}$
$\rho = 10.5 \text{ g/cc} = 10.5 \times 10^3 \text{ kg/m}^3$
$\sigma = 1.5 \text{ g/cc} = 1.5 \times 10^3 \text{ kg/m}^3$
$g = 9.8 \text{ m/s}^2$

Substituting the values:

$F_v = \dfrac{4}{3} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times (10^{-3})^3 \times (10.5 \times 10^3 - 1.5 \times 10^3) \times 9.8$

$F_v = \dfrac{4}{3} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 10^{-9} \times 9000 \times 9.8$

$F_v = 4 \times 22 \times 3000 \times \dfrac{9.8}{7} \times 10^{-9}$

$F_v = 88 \times 3000 \times 1.4 \times 10^{-9}$

$F_v = 88 \times 4200 \times 10^{-9}$

$F_v = 369600 \times 10^{-9} \text{ N}$

$F_v = 3696 \times 10^{-7} \text{ N}$

Comparing this with the given viscous force $3696 \times 10^{-x} \text{ N}$, we get:

$x = 7$

Answer: $7$

The potential energy at displacement $y$ is $U=\frac{1}{2} m \omega^2 y^2$
The kinetic energy is $K=E-U=\frac{1}{2} m \omega^2\left(a^2-y^2\right)=E-\frac{1}{2} m \omega^2 y^2$
Now at $y=\frac{a}{2}K=E-\frac{1}{2} m \omega^2\left(\frac{a^2}{4}\right)=E-\frac{E}{4}=\frac{3 E}{4}$

70895.subject: Biology
70895.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I - Gemmule is an internal bud formed in the body of coelenterate.
Statement II - The amoebocytes of the gemmule form protective covering membrane on the outerside.
In the light of above statements, choose the correct option given below:
options: Both statement I and statement II are correct.
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct.
70895.sol:
Statement I is incorrect because gemmules are internal buds formed for asexual reproduction in sponges (phylum Porifera), not in coelenterates. Coelenterates typically reproduce asexually through external budding.

Statement II is incorrect because a gemmule consists of a central mass of totipotent cells called archaeocytes, which are responsible for developing into a new sponge. The protective outer covering (consisting of spongin and spicules) is secreted by the amoebocytes (specifically spongioblasts and scleroblasts) of the parent sponge's mesohyl, not by cells belonging to the gemmule itself. The gemmule does not contain amoebocytes.

Therefore, both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.

Answer: Both statement I and statement II are incorrect.

71400.text: Which of the following term is best suited for the process, which involves production of offsprings by the formation and fusion of gametes?
71400.sol:
Amphimixis is the process of sexual reproduction which involves the formation and fusion of male and female gametes to produce offspring.

Apomixis is a type of asexual reproduction that mimics sexual reproduction but occurs without the fusion of gametes.

Apogamy is the development of a sporophyte directly from a gametophyte without fertilization.

Parthenocarpy is the development of fruit without fertilization, resulting in seedless fruits.

Answer: Amphimixis

71417.text: Diosgenin is primarily used in the manufacturing of------

Diosgenin is a phytosteroid sapogenin extracted from the tubers of Dioscorea species (wild yam). It serves as a crucial precursor for the semi-synthesis of various steroid hormones, most notably progesterone. Progesterone and its derivatives are key active ingredients in oral contraceptives. Therefore, diosgenin is primarily used in the manufacturing of birth control pills.

71600.subject: Chemistry
71600.text: Identify the substrate 'S' in the following reaction.
71600.sol:
The given reaction is a nucleophilic aromatic substitution where a leaving group on the benzene ring is replaced by an $-\text{OH}$ group from water to form 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (picric acid).

Aryl halides are generally unreactive towards nucleophilic substitution. However, the presence of strong electron-withdrawing groups (like $-\text{NO}_2$) at the ortho and para positions with respect to the halogen atom greatly increases their reactivity.

In 2,4,6-trinitrochlorobenzene, there are three $-\text{NO}_2$ groups at the ortho and para positions to the chlorine atom. This makes the ring highly electron-deficient and the $\text{C}-\text{Cl}$ bond highly susceptible to nucleophilic attack. Because of this extreme activation, the nucleophilic substitution can occur under very mild conditions, such as simply warming with water.

Reaction:
2,4,6-trinitrochlorobenzene + warm $\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2,4,6-trinitrophenol + \text{HCl}$

Therefore, the substrate 'S' is 2,4,6-trinitrochlorobenzene.

Answer: 2, 4, 6 - trinitrochlorobenzene

72332.subject: Physics
72332.text: There is a large difference between the frequencies of the external periodic force and the natural frequency of a body. The body will
options: vibrate with large amplitude at the frequency of external periodic force.
vibrate with small amplitude at the frequency of external periodic force.
vibrate with small amplitude at the own natural frequency.
72332.sol:
When an external periodic force is applied to a body, it executes forced vibrations. The body vibrates with the frequency of the applied external periodic force, not its natural frequency.

The amplitude of forced vibrations is given by $A = \dfrac{F_0}{m \sqrt{(\omega^2 - \omega_0^2)^2 + (b\omega/m)^2}}$, where $\omega$ is the frequency of the external force and $\omega_0$ is the natural frequency of the body.

Since there is a large difference between the frequency of the external periodic force and the natural frequency, the term $(\omega^2 - \omega_0^2)^2$ is very large.

Consequently, the amplitude $A$ of the vibration becomes very small. Thus, the body will vibrate with a small amplitude at the frequency of the external periodic force.

Answer: vibrate with small amplitude at the frequency of external periodic force.

73913.text: The menstrual cycle in females is controlled by hormones that are secreted by
73913.sol:
The menstrual cycle in females is regulated by the coordinated action of hormones from the hypothalamus, anterior pituitary gland, and ovaries.

The anterior pituitary gland secretes gonadotropins, namely Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH) and Luteinizing Hormone (LH), which regulate the ovarian cycle.

The ovaries secrete the steroid hormones estrogen and progesterone, which regulate the uterine cycle and exert feedback control on the pituitary gland.

Lacrimal glands secrete tears, sebaceous glands secrete sebum, and the prostate gland is a part of the male reproductive system.

Answer: Ovary and pituitary gland

75140.text:
Consider the following statements:
I. A Money Bill shall not be introduced in the Rajya Sabha.
II. The Rajya Sabha has no power to reject a Money Bill but can suggest amendment(s).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
75140.sol:
According to Article 109(1) of the Constitution of India, a Money Bill shall not be introduced in the Council of States (Rajya Sabha). Thus, Statement I is correct.

According to Article 109(2), after a Money Bill has been passed by the House of the People (Lok Sabha), it is transmitted to the Rajya Sabha for its recommendations. The Rajya Sabha has no power to reject or amend a Money Bill directly. It can only return the bill within a period of fourteen days with its recommendations (suggested amendments), which the Lok Sabha may either accept or reject. Thus, Statement II is also correct.

Both statements I and II are correct.

Answer: Both I and II

75205.text:
Which of the following statements with reference to soil forming processes is/are correct?
1. Translocation, enrichment, removal and transformation are different classes of soil forming processes
2. In translocation, fine particles are transported downward by eluviation and accumulate in lower horizons by illuviation
Select the answer using the code given below:
75205.sol:
Soil forming processes are broadly grouped into four classes: additions (enrichment), losses (removal), translocations, and transformations. Thus, the first statement is correct.

Translocation involves the movement of soil-forming materials through the developing soil profile. This occurs primarily by water moving through the soil, transferring materials from upper to lower portions. The removal of material from the upper horizon is called eluviation, and its deposition in the lower horizon is called illuviation. Thus, the second statement is also correct.

Both statements 1 and 2 are correct.

Answer: Both 1 and 2

76420.subject: Mathematics
76420.text:
Consider the following for the two (02) items that follow:
Let the curve $f(x) = |x - 3|$.

What is the area bounded by the curve $f(x)$ and $y = 3$?
76420.sol:
The given curve is $y = |x - 3|$ and the line is $y = 3$.

To find the points of intersection, we equate the two equations:

$|x - 3| = 3$

$x - 3 = 3$ or $x - 3 = -3$

$x = 6$ or $x = 0$

The points of intersection are $(0,3)$ and $(6,3)$. The vertex of the curve $y = |x - 3|$ is at $(3,0)$.

The area bounded by the curve and the line forms a triangle with vertices $(0,3)$, $(6,3)$, and $(3,0)$.

The length of the base of this triangle (along the line $y = 3$) is $6 - 0 = 6$ units.

The height of the triangle (perpendicular distance from the vertex to the base) is $3 - 0 = 3$ units.

The required area is given by:

Area $= \dfrac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$

Area $= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 3 = 9$ square units.

Answer: $9$ square units

77945.subject: Mathematics
77945.text: What is the number of odd integers between 1000 and 9999 with no digit repeated?
77945.sol:
Case I
When unit digit can be $1,3,5$ or $7 \&$ digit at thousand's place can be $1,2,3,4,5,6,7$ or 8 .
No. of ways digits can be filled are:
$\begin{array}{|l|l|l|l|}\hline$7 & 8 & 7 & 4 \\\hline\end{array}
Total no's $=7 \times 8 \times 7 \times 4=1568$.
Case II
When unit digit can be $9 \&$ digit at thousand's place can be $1,2,3,4,5,6,7$ or 8 .
No. of ways digits can be filled are:
$\begin{array}{|l|l|l|l|}\hline$8 & 8 & 7 & 1 \\\hline\end{array}
Total no's $=8 \times 8 \times 7 \times 1=448$.
Case III
When unit digit can be $1,3,5$ or $7 \&$ digit at thousand's place can be 9 .
No. of ways digits can be filled are:
$\begin{array}{|l|l|l|l|}\hline$1 & 8 & 7 & 4 \\\hline\end{array}
Total no's $=1 \times 8 \times 7 \times 4=224$.
$\begin{aligned} \therefore \quad \text{ Number of odd digits between } 1000 \& 9999 & \text{ with no } \\ \text{ digit repeated } & =1568+448+224 \\ & =2240 .\end{aligned}$

79028.text: What is the maximum value of $\sin 2 x \cdot \cos 2 x ?$
79028.sol:
$\begin{aligned} & y=\sin 2 x \cdot \cos 2 x \\ & \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{d}{d x}(\sin 2 x) \cdot \cos 2 x+\frac{d}{d x}(\cos 2 x) \cdot \sin 2 x\end{aligned}=\cos ^2 2 x-\sin ^2 2 x=\cos 4 x$
For maximum or minimum value
$\frac{d y}{d x}=0 \Rightarrow \cos 4 x=0\therefore 4 x=\frac{\pi}{2} \Rightarrow x=\frac{\pi}{2 \times 4}$
Now, $\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}=-4 \cdot \sin 4 x$
At $x=\frac{\pi}{2 \times 4}, \frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}=-4 \cdot \sin \frac{\pi}{2}=-4$.
$\therefore y$ is max. at $x=\frac{\pi}{2 \times 4}\begin{aligned} y_{\max } & =\sin 2\left(\frac{\pi}{2 \times 4}\right) \cdot \cos 2\left(\frac{\pi}{2 \times 4}\right) \\ & =\sin \frac{\pi}{4} \cdot \cos \frac{\pi}{4}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}$

Same number of chromosomes but twice the amount of DNA
Twice the number of chromosomes and four times the amount of DNA
Four times the number of chromosomes and twice the amount of DNA

S-phase (synthesis phase) is the part of the cell cycle in which DNA is replicated, but a number of chromosome does not change.

If a cell is diploid then after S phase DNA content in the cell will be 4 C and Chromosome in the cell will be 2 N.

While in a gamete,

DNA content in gamete = C

Chromosome in gamete = N

Hence, the Number of chromosome in a somatic cell will be twice than gamete while DNA content will be four times.

83054.subject: Physics
83054.text: In the measurement of viscosity of liquids using terminal velocity experiment, spherical balls of same radius but having different densities are used. The variation of the terminal velocity ($v$) with the ratio of density of spherical ball ($\sigma$) to density of the liquid ($\rho$), is best represented by :
83054.sol:
The terminal velocity $v$ of a spherical ball of radius $r$ and density $\sigma$ falling through a liquid of density $\rho$ and viscosity $\eta$ is given by Stokes' law:

$v = \dfrac{2r^2g}{9\eta}(\sigma - \rho)$

Rearranging the terms to express $v$ as a function of the ratio $\dfrac{\sigma}{\rho}$:

$v = \dfrac{2r^2g\rho}{9\eta} \left( \dfrac{\sigma}{\rho} - 1 \right)$

Let $y = v$ and $x = \dfrac{\sigma}{\rho}$. The equation becomes:

$y = k(x - 1)$

where $k = \dfrac{2r^2g\rho}{9\eta}$ is a positive constant.

This represents the equation of a straight line with a positive slope $k$ and an x-intercept at $x = 1$ (i.e., $v = 0$ when $\dfrac{\sigma}{\rho} = 1$).

Looking at the given graphs, only the second graph shows a straight line with a positive slope that intersects the horizontal axis at $\dfrac{\sigma}{\rho} = 1$.

Answer:

83068.subject: Physics
83068.text: Water rises to a height 'h' in capillary tube. If the length of capillary tube above the surface of water is made less than 'h', then:
options: water rises upto the top of capillary tube and stays there without overflowing.
water rises upto a point a little below the top and stays there.
water does not rise at all.
water rises upto the tip of capillary tube and then starts overflowing like a fountain.
83068.sol: It won't overflow. That should be obvious since doing so would create a constant flow, constantly using energy, but without any energy input. The same force that pulls the water along the inside of the capillary tube also holds it there when it reaches the end. This force doesn't just pull upward, it pulls the water along the glass. At a certain height, the weight of the water column balances this pull. In that case the pull is upward since there is water below but not above.

83611.subject: Physics
83611.text:
Steam at ${100}^{o}C$ is passed into $20g$ of water at ${10}^{o}C .$ When water acquires a temperature of ${80}^{o}C,$ the mass of water present will be:
[Take specific heat of water $= 1cal{g}^{- 1o}{C}^{- 1}$ and latent heat of steam $= 540cal{g}^{- 1} ]$
83611.sol:
Given: Specific heat of water ${S}_{w} = 1cal{g}^{- 1} ° {C}^{- 1}$, Latent heat of steam ${L}_{s} = 540cal{g}^{- 1}$

Let the mass of steam $= mg$

So heat lost in change of state from steam to water equal to sum of latent heat and heat use in raise of the temperature of water.

${Q}_{1} = m{L}_{s} + m{s}_{w} ∆ T$

${Q}_{1} = m \times 540 + m \times 1 \times ( 100 - 80 )$

${Q}_{1} = 540m + 20m = 560m$

Heat gained by water to change its temperature

${Q}_{2} = {m}_{w}{S}_{w} ∆ T$

${Q}_{2} = 20 \times 1 \times ( 80 - 10 ) = 1400$.

85159.text: The sixth mutant codon of beta globin gene causing polymerization of Haemoglobin and change in RBC shape is :
85159.sol:
Sickle cell anaemia is caused by the substitution of Glutamic acid (Glu) by Valine (Val) at the sixth position of the beta globin chain of the haemoglobin molecule.

This substitution of the amino acid occurs due to a single base substitution at the sixth codon of the beta globin gene from GAG to GUG.

The normal codon is GAG, which codes for Glutamic acid, while the mutant codon is GUG, which codes for Valine.

The presence of Valine leads to the polymerization of the mutant haemoglobin molecule under low oxygen tension, causing the change in the shape of the RBC from biconcave disc to an elongated sickle-like structure.

Answer: GUG
